blurb: A 19-year-old student with a part-time job: tight months, a housing deposit, a tuition payment plan and three scam-or-yield pitches.
intro: Zoe, 19, student with a part-time job. Opening: checking $600, savings $700, tuition fund $300. No debt, no crypto. Months 1 to 4: income $1,600, bills $1,500. Months 5 to 10: hours cut, income $1,300, bills $1,400. Month 8: $1,500 for the housing deposit and books. Month 12: first tuition payment of $1,500 plus a $45 plan fee; the other $3,000 is still owed afterward. The $45 plan fee and all other amounts are assumptions in this story.
name: Zoe Williams
plan: "Accessible bank balances" means checking + savings + tuition fund. They are accessible, not all free to spend: the tuition fund is earmarked for the month-12 payment.
Card: $800 limit, about 2% a month. If a bill is bigger than the room left on the card, the whole bill goes unpaid and a $35 late fee is added.

Harbor Vault is a fictional yield vault, not an insured account. In this story, buying or selling costs 0.5%; sales of crypto also cost a $19 on-chain fee per holding. In this story, a sale settles within the month.
Every purchase amount includes the 0.5% fee: the full amount leaves your cash and the asset receives the amount minus the fee.
